a.xlink:title: auth.users EXTERNAL: Supabase Auth. Google OAuth is primary; verified email/password is an optional secondary provider.
profiles Identity/contact record. It has no tenant role.
community_memberships Tenant authorization source. A role is valid only on an active, non-ended membership.

departments The 0019 columns above were missing from this diagram until 2026-08-09. status and is_active say the same thing to two readers; sync_department_status() writes each from the other, so neither can drift.
resident_invites Stores only hashes. Redemption requires the invitee verified Google email.

staff_assignments The 0019 columns above were missing from this diagram until 2026-08-09. staff_assignments_identity_check requires membership_id or display_name, so a row is always nameable on screen. (department_id, community_id) is a composite FK onto departments(id, community_id), which makes a cross-tenant row unrepresentable rather than merely forbidden.
service_providers A service person, global. Created by the holder of the profile, never by an administrator.

skills GLOBAL, unlike complaint_categories which is per-community. That asymmetry is what complaint_categories.skill_id exists to bridge, and it is why service_provider_skills can be written before anyone has been hired. 12 trades seeded by 0034.

worker_availability_rules 0036 - num_nonnulls(staff_assignment_id, service_provider_id) = 1. A roster name with no account keeps per-department hours; a registered service person keeps ONE set across every community that has hired them, because their week is not a fact about one of their four societies. Both set has no defined meaning, which is the case the num_nonnulls spelling catches and the naive one misses. 0039 gave it endpoints: PUT /worker/availability-rules replaces the provider-keyed half whole, and the roster-keyed half stays writable by nobody, because the person it describes has no account.

worker_unavailability 0036 - same one-subject rule as worker_availability_rules above. 0039 writes the provider-keyed half through POST /worker/unavailability. Overlapping rows are allowed on purpose: the dispatch sweep reads them with NOT EXISTS, so two blocks saying "away" say the same thing, and a uniqueness rule here would refuse "away all week, especially Tuesday".

complaints
RLS from 0031. Admins see the community queue, a resident sees their own: `is_community_admin(community_id) or is_own_membership(raised_by_membership_id)`. No write policy - raise_complaint, update_complaint, reopen_complaint and confirm_complaint_resolution are SECURITY DEFINER and authorize themselves.
`resolved` and `closed` are not synonyms. The association resolves; only the resident closes, through confirm_complaint_resolution.
The 0019 and 0020 columns above were missing from this diagram until 2026-08-04. They had been in the schema since those migrations; the omission was this file's.

complaint_events
Append-only. Written only by the complaint RPCs, never directly. 0031 adds `reopened` and `resolution_confirmed` to the event vocabulary.
A `comment_added` event is written for internal comments too, because this timeline was built for the admin screen. The resident detail endpoint drops those rows: an entry saying something was said, leading to a thread where nothing new is visible, is a worse leak than the comment would have been.

complaint_read_state
In the baseline from the start; nothing wrote to it until 0031. Per membership, so an admin opening a complaint cannot clear a resident marker. `complaint_overview.is_unread` is computed from it.

work_orders Un-parked from CONFLICT_RESOLUTIONS R16, which said to build nothing against this table. Extended additively rather than replaced, exactly as 0019 extended departments. ONE COMPLAINT MAY CARRY MANY: a failed visit is rescheduled and a reopened complaint goes to a different supervisor, and both are a second work order -- which is why the assignment is not columns on complaints, the smaller change that would have allowed only one scheduled visit per complaint. The lifecycle is written to complaint_events (job_created, job_scheduled, job_declined, job_assigned, job_cancelled) rather than to a parallel work_order_events table, and needed no migration because complaint_events.event_type is text with no CHECK.

work_order_assignments CARRIES work_order_assignments_no_overlap: exclude using gist (staff_assignment_id with =, tstzrange(scheduled_start_at, scheduled_end_at, `[)`) with &&) where (status = accepted and scheduled_start_at is not null). A person cannot be in two places at once, and the schema is where that is said. Same construct amenity_bookings has carried since 0001, and it needs btree_gist -- which is not a new requirement, since 0001 both installs the extension and declares an exclusion constraint that cannot exist without it. THE PARTIAL PREDICATE IS THE INTERESTING HALF: only accepted rows are constrained, so 0037 may offer one slot to several workers and let exactly one take it.
amenity_bookings The baseline uses a GiST exclusion constraint to prevent overlapping requested/approved times for an amenity.

notifications The durable record. Every user-visible event writes a row here first; SSE and Web Push are two deliveries of it, never the record of it. Written only by notify_member() or notify_profile(), in the same transaction as the change it describes. 0041 re-addressed it from a membership to a PERSON: a service provider who has registered and not yet been hired holds no membership anywhere, so under the 0030 shape there was no row that could tell them the answer to their own application. recipient_profile_id is always populated, including for the membership case, so ownership has one predicate everywhere. RLS: read policy recipient_profile_id = auth.uid(), no write policy, so marking read is mark_notification_read(). A row with no membership gets no SSE frame -- sse_events.community_id is not null.

push_subscriptions One row per BROWSER, not per person: a phone and a laptop are two. endpoint is unique across the table because the endpoint URL is the browser identity to the push service, so a shared device re-subscribing moves the row instead of duplicating it. 0041 changed the owner from a membership to a profile, which fixed a defect the uniqueness had been hiding: a person in two societies subscribing the same browser from the second one MOVED the row and silently stopped the first society pushes. RLS enabled with no policy (service_role only) -- p256dh_key and auth_key are encryption material. register_push_subscription() takes no owner argument at all; it reads auth.uid().
media Metadata only; object content is in external Supabase Storage.

sse_events Tenant-scoped live-update outbox, audience-scoped since 0028: a check constraint makes the three audiences mutually exclusive and complete, and the reader fails closed on anything it cannot classify. Browser clients consume the backend SSE projection, not database subscriptions. RLS enabled with no policy (0024), so only service_role reads it. EPHEMERAL — pruned every 15 minutes by prune_sse_events(), which is why nothing durable is built on it and notifications exists.
community_settings Settings screen toggles 3 and 4. Read through community_settings_overview.
community_billing_settings Settings screen toggles 1 and 2 plus invoice numbering. Written by update_billing_settings.
complaint_categories UQ (community_id, lower(btrim(name))) — categories are typed as free text, so Plumbing and plumbing are one category.
department_categories Which complaint categories a department claims. The baseline has no equivalent.
amenity_booking_guests Guests named on a booking. No membership reference: a guest is by definition not a member.
amenity_booking_charges Per-booking charge breakdown. The baseline booking_charges is written alongside it and kept populated.
amenity_financial_events Append-only. Money moves against a CHARGE, not a booking, so a refund can say which deposit it returned.
blacklisted_residents A reversible community-specific join blacklist. At most one active row per community and profile.

service_provider_skills Skills belong to the PERSON, not to a roster row. The "which communities need my trades" search has to run before anyone has hired them, which is exactly when they have no staff_assignment to hang a skill on. Supersedes staff_skills.

blacklisted_service_providers Deliberately NOT blacklisted_residents. That table is keyed on a profile and enforced inside search_joinable_communities, so reusing it would bar this person from LIVING here as a side effect of refusing to hire them.

staff_departures A request to leave, and the handover the approval is gated on. Before 0043 removal was one statement that said nothing about the work the person was holding -- an accepted work_order_assignments row survived a removal untouched, still pointing at tomorrow, addressed to a membership that had just ended. A pending row here freezes the dispatch sweep against that staff row and two triggers refuse any new booking against it, so the outstanding list can only get shorter. Approval is refused while it is non-empty; a BAR is the exception and releases the work to the engine instead.

service_applications An application and an invitation are one negotiation started from opposite ends, so they are one table. Accepting does the same three writes either way -- membership, staff_assignments row, decision -- in ONE transaction. Two tables would mean two inboxes and two chances for a hire to be half-done.

conversations One thread per (department, provider) pair. The thread outlives every application in it -- somebody who applied, was rejected, and applied again a year later is talking to the same department about the same work -- so it is keyed to the pair and has no foreign key to service_applications. There is deliberately NO conversation_participants table: participation is derivable (an admin or manager of the department, or that provider) and deriving it is exactly what the RLS policy computes.

conversation_messages TWO author columns, exactly one set (num_nonnulls = 1). Not one column, because the provider a manager most needs to reach is one who has NOT been hired yet and therefore holds no membership in this community at all -- the same fact that makes an invitation unnotifiable. Which column is written is decided by the THREAD rather than by the caller, so author_provider_id is not null reads as "the worker said this" even after they are hired and hold a membership too.

dm_threads Who may reach whom is dm_pair_allowed, one predicate behind both the recipients directory and the open: both active members, and either one is an admin or manager -- THE COMMITTEE IS THE ADMIN ROLE (USER_IDENTIFICATION.md) -- or they share a department. Residents reach the office, not each other; their worker contact is the job thread.

dispatch_tasks The engine at-LEAST-once, which is the opposite of what the push sender chose. push.py claims by marking a notification sent before it sends, so a crash loses a buzz rather than repeating one -- right for something that vibrates a phone at 3am, wrong here, because a dropped resident_timeout is a complaint left waiting forever with nobody coming. So claim_dispatch_batch takes a lease and every firing function is idempotent: each re-reads the work order and returns without writing if the world has already moved on. RLS is ENABLED WITH NO POLICY, following push_subscriptions (0030): machine bookkeeping, no client has a reason to read it, and the dispatcher runs on the service client which bypasses RLS. Rows are written by exactly one thing -- an after-insert-or-update trigger on work_orders that keeps this table in agreement with the job status -- so no future write path has to remember to arm a timer, and cancelling a job stops its timers without cancel_work_order knowing this table exists.

security_posts Where a guard stands. Written only by upsert_security_post, which requires gate_admin_community_for -- an admin, a manager, or a security membership whose roster row is ranked manager or supervisor. That last clause is the first place D3s rank-and-role split has to be honoured in code rather than described.

security_shifts work_order_assignments with the nouns changed -- same GiST exclusion constraint, same btree_gist dependency, same reason: a person cannot be in two places at once, and the schema is where that is said. THE PARTIAL PREDICATE IS WHERE THE TWO DIFFER AND IT HAS TO. Assignments constrain only accepted rows, because the dispatcher offers one slot to five workers and exactly one takes it -- constrain the offers and it can only ever ask one person. Nobody offers a shift to five guards, so there is no equivalent state and the predicate is everything except cancelled: a COMPLETED shift still occupied that evening, and a new one written over it is a rota error rather than a historical curiosity. Overlap is refused BY NAME in schedule_security_shift before the constraint refuses it by number, the pairing 4.13 arrived at.

material_movements US-3.3, replacing the paper register. A SEPARATE TABLE from water_tanker_logs rather than one typed table with a kind and a details jsonb (plan D12) -- and the reading confirms it: the two share not one column past the bookkeeping. is_returnable, expected_return_at and returned_at against tanker_number, volume_litres and supplier_name. One table would be null-heavy in both halves and would move validation out of the schema and into Python.
water_tanker_logs US-3.4, and the first thing in this product that touches water management at all.

security_incidents The form already exists and already writes to nothing. SecurityDashboard.jsx:166 collects a type, a location and details, and logIncident appends an interpolated STRING to an in-memory activity feed -- the same defect DECISIONS_NEEDED B2 names on the complaint assignee, one surface over. This is the table that string should always have gone into.

offline_reconcile_log WHY THE OFFLINE BUNDLE IS NOT SIGNED, WHICH PLAN D13 SAID IT WOULD BE. A signature the device verifies against a key the device holds is theatre -- the same person who can edit localStorage can delete the check beside it, because both are JavaScript on their machine. What is actually load-bearing is that an offline admission is PROVISIONAL UNTIL RECONCILED: reconcile_offline_entry re-runs the real verification and records the servers own verdict beside the devices claim, so a fabricated entry becomes a flagged row in an audit log rather than an admitted guest. This table is also why the replay branch cannot just re-verify: a second scan of one credential is a DEPARTURE, so replaying an admission twice would check the visitor out. The recorded verdict is returned untouched instead. Read policy is is_community_admin ALONE, not gate staff: the person whose entries are being checked is not the person the check is for.

service_signup_funnel_events The service-professional launch funnel, and deliberately not an experiment or a generic analytics framework. THE PRIMARY KEY IS THE WHOLE DESIGN: (visitor_id, event_name) is one row per visitor per step, so somebody who reloads the landing page twenty times is one cta_impression and the funnel counts people rather than page loads. Nothing joins it to a profile, because a funnel that could be joined to one would be a record of what a named person did before they had an account. RLS enabled with NO policy and every grant revoked including anon: the only writer is record_service_signup_funnel_event(), a definer function the unauthenticated endpoint calls.

department_skills The skills a department needs, chosen explicitly by an administrator or its manager. EMPTY BY DEFAULT -- a department inherits nothing from its categories. Inside search_hireable_service_providers the two paths are a UNION rather than a replacement, so a department that has picked no skills hires exactly as it did before this table existed. complaint_categories.skill_id (0034) remains the other half of the join between what a person can do and what a community needs done; this is the half somebody can curate directly.

staff_invitations A manager or supervisor an administrator has created but who has not signed in yet. THERE IS NO TOKEN AND NO REGISTRATION FLOW FOR LEADERSHIP: claim_staff_invitations matches on the email address at first sign-in, so the address IS the authorization. That is a single factor and it is stated rather than softened in docs/design/STAFF_PROVISIONING_DESIGN.md -- widening resident_invites, whose token stays a mandatory second factor, was the obvious move and the wrong one. update_staff_invitation is the typo recovery path the product owner chose over a claim code; it makes the accident recoverable and does nothing about the security case.

complaint_department_requests A supervisor saying a complaint belongs to another department, and the answer from their manager. A REQUEST IS A ROW RATHER THAN AN UPDATE because somebody who could push work out of their own department could empty it, and the department receiving it would have no say either way. Answered by the manager of from_department_id, never to_department_id -- authorizing on the destination would let the manager of B decide what A gives away. Read policy is can_supervise_department(from_department_id); there is no INSERT or UPDATE policy, so both writes are RPCs, the 0031 posture.
